en.bdb: Manmukh is like bronze and conch

verses.gurmukhi: ਉਜਲ ਕੈਹਾਂ ਚਿਲਕਣਾ ਥਾਲੀ ਜੇਵਣਿ ਜੂਠੀ ਹੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: aujal kaihaa(n) chilakanaa thaalee jevan jooThee hovai|

en.bdb: The bronze appears shining and bright. After the food eaten from the bronze-plate, it becomes impure.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜੂਠਿ ਸੁਆਹੂ ਮਾਂਜੀਐ ਗੰਗਾ ਜਲ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਲੈ ਧੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: jooTh suaahoo maa(n)jeeaai ga(n)gaa jal a(n)dhar lai dhovai|

en.bdb: Its impurity is cleaned by ashes and then it is washed in the water of Ganges.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਾਹਰੁ ਸੁਚਾ ਧੋਤਿਆਂ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਕਾਲਖ ਅੰਤਿ ਵਿਗੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: baahar suchaa dhotiaa(n) a(n)dhar kaalakh a(n)t vigovai|

en.bdb: Washing cleans externally but the blackness goes on to remain inside the inner core of heat.

verses.gurmukhi: ਮਨਿ ਜੂਠੇ ਤਨਿ ਜੂਠਿ ਹੈ ਥੁਕਿ ਪਵੈ ਮੁਹਿ ਵਜੈ ਰੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: man jooThe tan jooTh hai thuk pavai muh vajai rovai|

en.bdb: The conch is impure outwardly and internally both because when blown, the spit goes in it. When it chimes, in fact it weeps because of the impurities in it.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਗੁਰ ਸਬਦੁ ਸੁਣਿ ਕਪਟ ਸਨੇਹੀ ਗਲਾਂ ਗੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: saadhasa(n)gat gur sabadh sun kapaT sanehee galaa(n) govai|

en.bdb: Listening to the Word in the holy congregation the cheat talks nonsensically.

verses.gurmukhi: ਗਲੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਪਤਿ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਖੰਡੁ ਖੰਡੁ ਕਰਿ ਸਾਉ ਨ ਭੋਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: galee tirapat na hoviee kha(n)dd kha(n)dd kar saau na bhovai|

en.bdb: But by mere talking, none gets satisfied, as by mere uttering word sugar one cannot have his mouth sweet.
If one is to eat butter, one should not go churning water, i.e. mere talks cannot produce the right results.
